column1: # Fixup order for tools/fixorder.py: object stem, then every fixup of the object as a data
# offset (hex, from the start of its code segment), in the order TLINK must see them.
# HPSHRINK (src/heap/HPSHRINK.C, image 0xE4D8..0xE5BD). TLINK.EXE's relocation table lists
# entries #119-#122 as E507h (SHRINK_HEAP_FULLY's far call to SHRINK_HEAP_TO,
# (fixup at offset 2Dh, its segment word at 2Fh), then E4DDh, E4FCh and E514h (the DGROUP loads at 5h, 24h and 3Ch).
# The file is compiled through TASM 2.51 (-B -TjNOSMART), which gives every byte and writes
# the fixups as 5h, 24h, 3Ch, 2Dh. The same module and the same order are in BCC.EXE and
# CPP.EXE; cpp20 (tools/fixorder.tsv and docs/FINDINGS.md there) tested Turbo C 2.01, BC 2.0,
# Turbo C++ 1.01, TASM 1.0/2.0/2.51 and TLINK 3.0/4.0, and no source gives the order:
# TASM only puts a far call first when its target is declared before the call, and here the
# target is a later function of the same file. Split files cannot give it either (TLINK
# keeps object order). Only the far call moves; the other fixups keep TASM's order.
